defs.text: Having life; something alive.
defs.example: The post office will not ship live animals.

defs.text: A live firearm or explosive is able to cause harm.
defs.example: The air force practices dropping live bombs on the uninhabited island.

defs.text: d or energized with electricity, usually meaning that the wire or circuit can cause an electric shock or electrocution if someone or an animal comes in contact with it.
defs.example: Use caution when working near live wires.

defs.text: A live bet is a bet that can be raised by the person betting.
defs.example: Tommy's blind was live, so he was given the option to raise.

defs.text: To be alive; to have life.
defs.example: He's not expected to live for more than a few months.

defs.text: To have permanent residence somewhere.
defs.example: I live at 256 Oak Avenue.

defs.text: To survive, to continue.
defs.example: Her memory lives in that song.

defs.text: You use miss before an unmarried woman's name, usually the last name or the full name.
defs.example: Miss Brakel, the doctor will see you now.

defs.text: You call a young woman miss when you don't know her name.
defs.example: Excuse me, miss, I think you dropped this.

defs.text: If you miss something, you don't hit it.
defs.example: I missed the target.

defs.text: If you miss someone or something when they are gone or away, you wish they were there with you.
defs.example: I miss you so much. When are you coming home?

defs.text: If you miss an event, you aren't able to go.
defs.example: I'm going to have to miss the party because I can't find a babysitter.

defs.text: If you miss something, you aren't able to get on it in time.
defs.example: I'm sorry I'm late; I missed the bus.

defs.text: Prepared.
defs.example: Let's get ready to rumble!
